As the No. 19 Ole Miss football team was upset by the unranked Oklahoma Sooners on Sunday afternoon, 24-17, the conversation around the game was about how the contest was moved from Saturday. While Oklahoma head coach Brent Venables called it ‘insensitive’ to move the Ole Miss football matchup because of the fans, Pete Golding has his own thoughts on the situation. The reason for the change was that the Rebels and other college football teams had their flight plans disrupted after a nationwide ground stop by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) . There was no doubt transgressions on the side of the Sooners, as the program questioned if the Rebels exhausted every measure to get their team in Norman, Oklahoma, on time. With the game moved to Sunday, Golding said after the loss that he promised that “nobody was more frustrated than our team.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “I promise you, nobody was more frustrated than our team that got to a facility at 7:45 on Friday morning. And we’re sitting on buses for three hours and sitting under a stadium and got called back and in meeting rooms, and we’re holding them,” Golding said, via Joe Mussato. “There was nobody more frustrated; I can assure you they didn’t want to wait another day. You know, everybody wanted to exhaust everything that we could to get here Friday night. You know, they called us and told us we weren’t able to do that.” “I promise you, nobody was more frustrated than our team.” Ole Miss coach Pete Golding on the tension regarding the schedule change: pic.twitter.com/PN3BQbpLtv — Joe Mussatto (@joe_mussatto) November 15, 2026 Ole Miss football’s Pete Golding continues on moving the game to Sunday Golding continued about the Ole Miss football program having to move the game, with him saying that it reminded him of when COVID-19 halted the sports world and how teams had to work around it. “We didn’t get to decide this, we didn’t get to choose this, but it is what it is…Let’s go show up. And we better be ready to go because I know they will be,” Golding said. The Rebels would end up losing in a disappointing fashion to the Sooners, as the program looks to get back in the winning column next Saturday against the Wofford Terriers. item.title: Texans’ Kamari Lassiter is completely dumbfounded at penalty that cost him crucial INT
item.description: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Texans’ Kamari Lassiter is completely dumbfounded at penalty that cost him crucial INT appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Houston Texans fought a close contest against the Cleveland Browns. It seemed as if Houston would leave this game with a victory. Kamari Lassiter came up with what looked like quite the interception. This was until the yellow flag hit the field. Lassiter was flagged for unnecessary roughness on the play. He did make contact with the receiver as he made an attempt to disrupt the pass, leading to the flag. After the game, the Texans star expressed his issues with the call. “It’s very frustrating, I mean, because as a player, it leaves you with a lot of indecision. I don’t know what I’m supposed to do, am I supposed to let him catch it? I’m trying to go for the ball. If he’s touching the ball, I’m trying to violently get the ball out of his hands. We play a violent sport, I don’t think that, I don’t know, I’m confused,” Lassiter said, via KPRC2 reporter Aaron Wilson. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Had Lassiter’s interception stood, the Texans would have had the ball late in the game and with the lead. However, the Browns retained possession. Two plays later, Quinshon Judkins found the endzone to give Cleveland a 27-24 lead. The Texans would get the ball back following that score. But they were unable to do anything with it. Houston failed to score at all as they dropped their sixth game of the season on Sunday. This is certainly a brutal loss for Houston to process. They now sit at 3-6 with fading playoff hopes. item.title: 'Couldn't get worse': Klopp calls for change in FIFA leadership
item.description: Germany coach Jurgen Klopp has called for a change in FIFA leadership. (Pedja Milosavljevic) Germany coach Jurgen Klopp called on Sunday for an end to Gianni Infantino's time as FIFA president, saying he "did not think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter." Speaking in Berlin ahead of Monday's Nations League clash with the Netherlands, Klopp said the next candidate for football's global governing body should have the game's interests at heart. "I've been following football for many years. There are people who are much more knowledgeable about this than I am. But I think most people now agree a change would make a lot of sense," Klopp said. "I didn't think things could get worse after Sepp Blatter, but someone has managed to do just that." President of FIFA from 1998, Blatter resigned in disgrace in 2015 amid corruption allegations, including accusations he had sought to buy votes for his presidency. Charges were brought against Blatter who was eventually cleared in two trials, but was banned from football by FIFA's ethics committee. Klopp added: "Regarding Gianni Infantino, surely the next person to come along can do a better job." Swiss Infantino succeeded Blatter as FIFA president in 2016 and has come under heavy criticism for a series of decisions and proposals, including his plan to sell off part of the commercial rights of the World Cup and creating a 'Peace Prize' award for US President Donald Trump. "There are people who truly care about the future of football -- people who aren't driven by financial interests," said Klopp. "If someone like that were to step up -- if someone like that were to become president -- I think that would be a significant improvement." "There are surely people who care deeply about the future of football and have no financial interests in it." The next election for FIFA president takes place in March 2027. Only former Swiss footballer Ramon Vega and Japan's Kozo Tashima have announced their intention to run against Infantino although Arsene Wenger has also been mentioned. Klopp did not discuss the other candidates, but said: "I've heard something about Arsene Wenger. Not sure if that's true or false, but he's a good man." dwi/td/pb

item.title: Rangers acquire struggling depth goalie Soderblom from Blackhawks
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The goalie depth chart in the New York Rangers organization received yet another minor reshuffling Sunday, when they acquired Arvid Soderblom from the Chicago Blackhawks in exchange for Spencer Martin . Soderblom will swap places with Martin on the Hartford Wolf Pack roster in the American Hockey League. The move nets the Rangers a goalie four years younger than Martin, and one who has 44 more games of NHL experience. The 27-year-old native of Sweden, struggled mightily for the woeful Blackhawks this season. In five games (four starts) for the Blackhawks, Soderblom was winless (0-3-1), with a 4.67 goals-against average and .842 save percentage in a backup role behind Spencer Knight. Chicago (5-13-2) has the second worst points percentage (.300) in the NHL. Soderblom played well in two starts for AHL Rockford after the Blackhawks sent him to the minors this past week. He won each game, allowed two goals total, and had a .957 save percentage. He will now share the net with 22-year-old goalie Callum Tung in Hartford. His acquisition gives the Rangers a more viable No. 3 goalie on the depth chart. New York had little faith in Martin, who’s 31 and didn’t exactly excel in the NHL last season when Igor Shesterkin landed on IR for a month with a lower-body injury in January. Soderblom played more than 30 games twice in the NHL, and owns a 3.65 GAA and .885 save percentage in 117 games over parts of six seasons with the Blackhawks. Rangers goalie shuffle continues with acquisition of Arvid Soderblom The trade occurred a few hours after the Rangers officially placed Shesterkin on season-ending injured reserve. Shesterkin sustained a severe knee injury Oct. 9 that requires surgery. The Rangers previously announced that the 30-year-old will miss the rest of the season, but up until Sunday, Shesterkin remained on long-term injured reserve. Now, he officially can’t play again until the 2027-28 season. After his injury, the Rangers relied heavily on 24-year-old rookie Dylan Garand because veteran backup Joonas Korpisalo was already out for a month due to a foot infection. Martin was recalled from Hartford to back up Garand, and then was replaced by veteran James Reimer, who played one game before the Rangers terminated his contract more than a week ago upon Korpisalo’s return. Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect So, yes, there’s been quite the game of musical chairs going on this season with goalies in the Rangers organization. item.title: England topple Spain as Belgium smash Italy to reach Nations League quarters
item.description: Harry Kane celebrates sending England on their way to a famous win against Spain (Thomas COEX) England ended Spain's unbeaten run in competitive matches at 44 on Sunday, beating the world champions 3-2 on their own patch, while Belgium thumped Italy 4-1 to join France in the Nations League quarter-finals. Thomas Tuchel's team win Group A3, level on 15 points with Spain, after the hugely impressive win in Madrid in which La Roja were for long periods made to look a shadow of the team which won the World Cup. But the Three Lions ended up down to 10 men and hanging on by their finger nails before inflicting on Spain a first defeat in a competitive fixture since March 2023. Asked by ITV whether this was England's best performance of his reign as coach, Tuchel said: "Under the circumstances against who and where we played, yeah." "(We showed) what we are made of and what we can do," added Tuchel, saying his team were motivated by their third place at the World Cup. "We are always ready to push our limits. We had our best result in 60 years and we weren't happy with it. It's impressive what we did in the last two camps." Harry Kane put the away side deservedly ahead on the stroke of half time, netting from the penalty spot, his record-extending 93rd England goal. Ezri Konsa struck just after the break before Ben White gave England a barely-believable lead in the 57th minute when he latched onto Jude Bellingham's pass and finished between Unai Simon's legs. England needed that cushion. Moments later they found themselves a man down when Elliot Anderson hauled backed Lamine Yamal in the box, conceding a penalty and a red card. Mikel Oyarzabal slotted home the spot-kick with Spain's first shot on target to set up a grandstand finish and bring back memories of England's collapse against Argentina which cost them a place in the World Cup final. Those jitters intensified when Nico Williams slammed home Lamine Yamal's inch-perfect cross with 15 minutes remaining, but England just about held out under a Spanish onslaught. - Belgium rout Italy - Sitting third in Group A1 ahead of kick-off and needing a win to qualify for the last eight, Belgium had their backs up against the wall when Francesco Pio Esposito volleyed Italy ahead in the 11th minute. But Belgium blew Italy away in the following quarter of an hour, with Maxim De Cuyper and Nathan Ngoy bundling the hosts ahead before Jeremy Doku slalomed through the Azzurri defence and confidently shot home. Mark van Bommel's team deservedly claimed a spot in the quarters and made sure the scoreline reflected the balance of play when one of many attacks against an open Italy defence ended with Diego Moreira slotting home with 10 minutes remaining. A dismal night for Italy, who were top of the group after beating France last time out and just needed a draw to go through, was made even worse when Senne Lammens saved Esposito's weak late penalty. item.title: 'Big Noon Kickoff' heading to Ferris State for start of DII playoffs
item.description: The big dogs in college football reside in Big Rapids. And, now, "Big Noon Kickoff" is coming to town. "Big Noon Kickoff," Fox's college football pregame show, has announced that it will broadcast from the campus of Ferris State on Saturday, Nov. 21, for the start of the Division II playoffs. It marks the first trip to a Division II school for "Big Noon Kickoff," and the trip comes after Ferris State set a Division II record with its 41st consecutive victory. Ferris State beat Roosevelt, 63-20, in the regular-season finale Saturday, Nov. 20, to take the all-time record by itself. Ferris State had been tied with rival Grand Valley State with 40 in a row. "I'm so proud of our players and coaches for all the work they have put in to make this happen," Ferris State head coach Tony Annese said Saturday. "This takes a commitment from everyone associated with our program and Bulldog Athletics. It's awesome to see the joy on their faces in a moment like this and the support we've received has been outstanding from everyone." Ferris State football hasn't lost a game since the 2024 playoffs. It has won back-to-back Division II national championships, and this week, it embarks on its quest for a threepeat after an 11-0 regular season. The Bulldogs, led by 20 seniors, are the No. 1 seed in their region, and they open the playoffs against Truman State from Missouri at noon Nov. 21 at Ferris State's Top Taggart Field. And "Big Noon Kickoff" will be there it all. Fox's flagship college football show, which launched in 2019, will broadcast live from campus from 10 a.m. until noon. This will be the third trip to Michigan for "Big Noon Kickoff" this season. It broadcast from Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor twice, for the 17-10 win over Oklahoma on Sept. 12 and the 13-6 overtime loss to Indiana on Oct. 24 . ESPN's "College GameDay," the older rival to the Fox show which debuted in 1994, has never been to a Division II location, though it has broadcast from Football Championship Subdivision schools and one Division III site. The only time either of the shows broadcast in Michigan from a campus other than Michigan or Michigan State was in 2016, when "GameDay" broadcast from Western Michigan on Nov. 19 that year during a season in which the Broncos went undefeated in the regular season, won a Mid-American Conference championship and played in the Cotton Bowl. Fox's "Big Noon Kickoff" broadcast team features analysts Urban Meyer, Mark Ingram II, Matt Leinart and Brady Quinn, host Rob Stone, and reporter Chris Fallica. "I've always said my favorite show locations are places we've either never been or haven't been for a long time," Fallica posted on X (formerly Twitter) after the Ferris State announcement. "This certainly qualifies. "Looking forward to Saturday!" The Division II football playoffs consist of 32 teams, with the championship game set for Dec. 19, at McKinney ISD Stadium in McKinney, Texas. item.description: NEW YORK — Gotham FC did its best to make the most of its relocated semifinal. Unfortunately for the reigning NWSL champions, Kansas City stole the show. On a chilly fall evening on Randall’s Island, the Kansas City Current defeated Gotham 2–1 with an 89th-minute game-winner to book a ticket to the NWSL title game in Washington. The Current will face the hometown Washington Spirit , which beat the Utah Royals on Saturday. Facing poor pitch conditions, Gotham ultimately decided to move the match from its usual home stadium in New Jersey to the 5,000-seat Icahn Stadium on New York City parkland in the East River. Gotham is a tenant of MLS club New York Red Bulls at Sports Illustrated Stadium in Harrison, N.J., and a combination of rugby matches and soccer games tore up the pitch over the past few weeks. The NWSL had previously fined Gotham $10,000 for pitch conditions for the final game of the regular season, and players and coaches blasted playing conditions after the Nov. 8. quarterfinal. With a Red Bulls friendly against Mexican side Club América scheduled for Saturday night—during which a fight broke out —Gotham decided to move to Icahn, which has a pitch donated by its future landlord , MLS’s New York City FC. On Sunday, Gotham organized ferries, buses, and watch parties for the fans, chartering boats and covering bar tabs. After the games, Gotham star Midge Purce said club owners have “done absolutely everything they could possibly do to make the best situation for us.” Purce, who called the field at Sports Illustrated Stadium “inexcusable,” said the pitch at Icahn had “no effect on performance” on Sunday. “I think it was the right decision to come here, I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable,” Gotham coach Juan Carlos Amorós said Sunday evening. item.title: Boston Celtics spoil Cooper Flagg homecoming, rout Dallas Mavericks, 131-94
item.description: BOSTON — NBA games are rarely decided in the first quarter, however, a Sunday afternoon showdown between the Boston Celtics and the Dallas Mavericks might be an exception. Boston blitzed Dallas in the first frame, outscoring its Western Conference opponent 42-9 to open the 131-94 victory at TD Garden. The Celtics gave up just 2 field goals through 12 minutes of play, which is the lowest amount of made shots they've ever allowed in the first quarter of a game in franchise history. Boston continued to impress from there, as it held a 67-37 lead heading into halftime after shooting a blistering 50 percent from the field. Although the C's got production from almost every one of their players, star forward Jayson Tatum led the way with a game-high 32 points. He also recorded 6 rebounds and 6 assists in 30 minutes of action. Meanwhile, the Mavericks were nowhere near as productive. They were on the second night of a back-to-back and missed the presence of star point guard Kyrie Irving, who was sidelined due to injury management. Star forward Cooper Flag notched 17 points in his second game ever in Boston — just 3 hours away from his hometown of Newport, Maine. Flagg had a homecoming to forget, though, tallying 3 turnovers in 27 minutes and missing 10 of his 15 shots from the floor. Following the 37-point blowout, the Celtics are 11-2 on the season and remain in first place in the Eastern Conference. They'll look to build upon their six-game winning streak in less than 24 hours when they host the 5-7 Orlando Magic at TD Garden on Monday night. item.title: Fox's 'Big Noon Saturday' at Ferris State for first D-II broadcast
item.description: A day after Ferris State football set the NCAA Division II record with its 41 st consecutive victory, the school reportedly got another historic win. Fox’s “Big Noon Saturday” is reportedly headed to Big Rapids for its morning kickoff show on Saturday, Nov. 21, ahead of the Bulldogs opening the Division II playoffs at Top Taggart Field at 1 p.m. against Truman State. The news was first reported by Brett McMurphy of On3 . MAKING HISTORY: Ferris State makes NCAA history with record 41st straight win It’s the first time in its eight seasons that the pregame show, featuring Rob Stone, Urban Meyer, Matt Leinart, Brady Quinn and Mark Ingram II, has spent a Saturday on a D-II campus. ESPN’s move venerated show, “College GameDay,” has also never broadcast from a D-II campus. The Bulldogs received a 1-seed in their region in the 32-team field as they go for their fifth national title in six years, as well as attempting to become just the second program with three straight D-II titles (North Alabama, 1993-95). A win over Truman would send the Bulldogs into the second round to face either Findlay (Ohio) or Augustana (South Dakota). On the other side of Ferris’ region, however, wait a trio of Michigan rivals: Grand Valley State faces 2-seed Northwood in Midland at 1 p.m. Saturday; the winner of that game faces the winner between Minnesota State and Michigan Tech, with the game to be played in Houghton at 1 p.m. Saturday. The Huskies are making just their third NCAA Tournament appearance, and first since 2014. Ferris, meanwhile, is making its 12 th consecutive NCAA appearance. Ferris State last lost in its 2024 season opener, to Pittsburg State (of Kansas) on Aug. 31, 2024. The next week, the Bulldogs wiped out Lake Erie, 56-3, to start its record run. The 799-day streak has included 20 GLIAC wins as well as nine NCAA playoff victories, including title game wins over Valdosta State in 2024 and Harding in 2025. The Bulldogs, coached by Tony Annese, are coming off a pair of GLIAC-clinching wins (against Wayne State in Detroit and Roosevelt) by a combined score of 143-20. Saturday’s victory in Big Rapids snapped a tie with Grand Valley State for the D-II record and also moved Ferris State into second for the longest streak among Division I (FBS- or FCS-level) and Division II programs, passing Washington’s 40-game run from 1908-14 and GVSU’s 40-game run from 2005-07. Oklahoma, at 47 wins from 1953-57, is the FBS-level record holder, while North Dakota State owns the FCS-level mark at 39 wins from 2017-20. The longest streak in NCAA football, however, belongs to Division III Mount Union, which won 55 straight from 2000-03. Another title for Ferris State – with the D-II championship game set for McKinney, Texas, on Dec. 19 – would mean five wins, putting the Bulldogs just three wins next season from passing the Sooners for the second-longest NCAA streak. item.description: SALT LAKE CITY — The San Jose Sharks are still trying to find their game. Good thing, veterans Dmitry Orlov and Mason Marchment are finding theirs. Orlov matched his career-high with four points on Saturday, notching a goal and three assists. Marchment had an assist and scored the shootout winner in a 6-5 victory over the Utah Mammoth . It wasn’t just about the counting stats: According to Stathletes, Orlov, offensively, led the San Jose Sharks with eight Passes Leading to Shots. Defensively, he had three Turnovers Forced, tying Darnell Nurse for the team blueline lead. Marchment was third on the Sharks with nine Successful Passes Under Pressure, trailing just Ivar Stenberg ’s 11 and Macklin Celebrini ’s 10. His two Inner Slot Shots, a point of focus for how the big winger could help the San Jose Sharks get out of their early-season swoon, tied Celebrini and Tyler Toffoli for the team lead. These are All Situations stats. You could see a lot of this come together in San Jose’s fourth and fifth goals. On Eric Pohlkamp ’s first-career NHL goal, it was Orlov (9) that sticked the puck away from Daniil But (50), initiating the Celebrini (71) rush. On Orlov’s knuckleball goal, Marchment uses his 6-foot-4 frame to keep the puck away from a swarming Zac Jones (15). Five Mammoth are watching Marchment strongside, and he’s able to rim the puck to the weakside to Collin Graf (51). Because of Marchment’s puck protection and Graf’s quick pass, Orlov has space, a long runway to shoot. It was a sloppy win for San Jose, but for the Sharks to turn their season around, they’ll need veterans like Orlov and Marchment to get going. There’s no doubt, both have struggled at times this season.
